display: Ho Chi Minh City — Saigon Waterbus

partner_context.their_ambition: Ho Chi Minh City is building a green public-transport network — electric buses across the city and a Saigon River water-bus that already carries commuters and visitors on Line 1 while the roads sit in chronic gridlock. The ambition is to grow the river into a real public mode as the city decarbonises its transport.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the zero-emission, foiling upgrade to the water-bus HCMC already runs. The same Line 1 stations — Bach Dang in the centre, Binh An, Thanh Da and Linh Dong upriver — served by fast, near-silent, low-wake foiling ferries: faster river commutes with no diesel wake on the Saigon River.

hero.eyebrow: Authority proposal · Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam · Saigon Waterbus
hero.title: Navier × Saigon Waterbus — the Saigon River, on foils
hero.subtitle: A zero-emission foiling layer on the city's river bus: faster commutes along the Saigon River, cleaner air, and a real public alternative to the gridlock as HCMC goes green.
hero.what_we_do_together: HCMC brings the Saigon Waterbus network, the wharves and the green-transport mandate; Navier brings the foiling-electric fleet, captain training and certification path. Together we run the same river the city already uses — faster, quieter and zero-emission — extending the green-transport push HCMC has already begun.

why_now: HCMC is rolling out electric buses across the city and has committed to converting public transport to green energy. Saigon Waterbus Line 1 is live along the river, with further lines planned under the city's water-transit development. The pull and the policy exist today — a foiling-electric layer is the fast, low-wake next step for the river.
multimodal_fit: Navier slots into the existing Saigon Waterbus — Bach Dang Wharf in District 1, Binh An and Thanh Da along the river, and Linh Dong upriver in Thu Duc — taking the high-frequency commuter reaches while conventional water-bus vessels keep heavier runs. Riders step from bus and metro straight onto a foil up the river.

journeys_unlocked.label: Bach Dang ↔ Binh An
journeys_unlocked.today: The trip out of the centre means slow, congested roads even at off-peak.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: The core Line 1 reach from downtown, flown clear of the water — fast, near-silent, zero-emission.

journeys_unlocked.label: Binh An ↔ Thanh Da
journeys_unlocked.today: A river-side stretch that still forces commuters onto gridlocked roads today.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A quick, clean hop along the Saigon River — low-wake and quiet past the riverbank.

journeys_unlocked.label: Thanh Da ↔ Linh Dong
journeys_unlocked.today: The upriver run to Thu Duc is a long, slow road trip through the growing city.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A fast upriver connection to Thu Duc — zero-emission and smooth on the water.

journeys_unlocked.label: Bach Dang ↔ Linh Dong (Line 1 through-run)
journeys_unlocked.today: End to end, Line 1 today is a leisurely river-bus or a congested road journey.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: The full Line 1 through-run at foiling speed — a genuine downtown–Thu Duc commuter link.

differentiation.why_navier: The platform is proven in service and purpose-built for exactly this job: 10x more efficient than a planing hull, low-wake (critical on a busy working river), near-silent, and zero-emission. It turns a scenic water-bus into a fast public commuter mode and extends HCMC's green-transport push onto the Saigon River.

proof_points.claim: The Saigon Waterbus is a live public river service.
proof_points.evidence: Line 1 (Bach Dang – Linh Dong, ~10.8 km) has operated on the Saigon River since 2017; further lines are planned.

proof_points.claim: HCMC is going green on transport.
proof_points.evidence: 25 new electric bus routes from 2025 and a city commitment to convert public transport to green energy.

proof_points.claim: The platform is proven in service.
proof_points.evidence: 10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out.

objections.concern: Can a foiling ferry work on the busy Saigon River?
objections.response: Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal at the existing wharves, flies above the chop and traffic wake for a smoother ride, and its low wake protects the riverbank on a heavily-used working river.

objections.concern: Is this affordable for a public service?
objections.response: Foiling-electric is ~10x more efficient than a diesel planing hull, so fuel — the largest operating cost — falls sharply; the same public budget runs more frequent crossings.

objections.concern: Does this replace the water-bus people use today?
objections.response: No — it's a faster layer above it. The existing water-bus keeps running; the foiling fleet adds speed and zero-emission capacity on the busiest reaches.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling-electric fleet, captain training, and the maintenance and certification path, aligned to Vietnam Register maritime requirements.
the_ask.partner_brings: The Saigon Waterbus route map, the wharves, the green-transport mandate, and the water-transit expansion plan.
the_ask.next_step: Pick the first Line 1 reach for a foiling-electric public pilot and align it with HCMC's green-transport rollout.

close.body: Ho Chi Minh City already runs a river bus and is electrifying its transport. Navier is how the river becomes a fast, clean commuter mode — giving riders a quick, quiet, zero-emission trip up the Saigon, and giving a fast-growing city a real alternative to its gridlock on the water.

end_state.headline: A zero-emission foiling layer along the Saigon River water-bus.
end_state.addressable_footprint: The Saigon Waterbus network from downtown District 1 upriver to Thu Duc — re-platformed onto foiling-electric vessels — with room to grow onto the city's planned further water-bus lines.

steady_state.total_corridors: Line 1 from Bach Dang to Linh Dong, and the city's planned further river lines
steady_state.platform_mix: Pioneer II across the river network
steady_state.the_opportunity: A fast, zero-emission public river service for one of Southeast Asia's fastest-growing cities.

end_state.narrative: Steady state is a decarbonised Saigon River: the water-bus grown into a fast, near-silent, low-wake foiling commuter mode — extending the green-transport network HCMC has already begun.
